# Predicting {-}

<!-- SCAFFOLD: signposting only. Eliot to expand -- what a prediction run needs
     from a fitting run, how climate projections enter, and what the outputs mean.
     See #2. -->

Prediction is the second stage.
It takes the models estimated in [Fitting] and applies them to a landscape,
producing ignition, escape and spread probabilities that vary with climate and
vegetation as a simulation proceeds.

The chapters mirror the fitting ones.
`fireSense_dataPrepPredict` prepares the covariates a prediction run needs, and
`fireSense_IgnitionPredict`, `fireSense_EscapePredict` and
`fireSense_SpreadPredict` apply the corresponding fitted sub-models.
The `fireSense` module itself ties these together into a simulated fire regime.

Because the sub-models are sensitive to climate and vegetation, a prediction run
is normally coupled to a vegetation model rather than run in isolation --
see [Integration with LandR Biomass].
